ghs.en: Kiri: "You OK?"
Miki: "...hm... I'm alright..."

rows.jp: 美希の涙をぬぐったのは、霧のハンカチだった。
rows.en: It is Kiri's handkerchief that wipes away Miki's tears.

ghs.en: Kiri had wiped off Miki's tears with her handkerchief.

rows.en: The two of them, pressed close.

ghs.en: Those two are nestled up close.

rows.en: There is no room for me between them.

ghs.en: There isn't any space in between them.

rows.jp: 俺は懐中電灯で、先頭を歩く。
rows.en: I walk in front with the flashlight.

ghs.en: I walk in the lead, with my flashlight.

rows.jp: なぜ美希はここに来たがったのか。
rows.en: Why did Miki want to come here?

ghs.en: Why did Miki want to come here?
Why with the three of us?
And why... was she crying?

rows.jp: ……美希もいろいろ抱えているには違いない。
rows.en: ...Miki must be carrying all sorts of things too.

ghs.en: ...Miki too has lots and lots of baggage, no mistake.

rows.jp: まあ、プライベートはどうでもいいや。
rows.en: Well, her private life is none of my concern.

ghs.en: Well, the private stuff is none of my business.

rows.jp: そういや、ここは祠の近くだったな。
rows.en: Come to think of it, we're near the shrine.

ghs.en: On that, the hokora was close to here wasn't it.

rows.en: I might as well take a quick look.

ghs.en: Should I just give a quick look?

rows.jp: 「霧、ちょっと俺、寄ってくところがあるんで……」
rows.en: “Kiri, there's somewhere I want to stop by for a minute...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Kiri, there's this place I'd like to drop by just a bit, so..."
I hand over the flashlight.
Taichi: "Welll see ya."
Kiri: "Eh... ah, wait!"
Miki: "Ah, over there's... danger..."
And then I,
Taichi: "I finally larrived."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese uses a colloquial ra-dropping form of 'could come.' The English creates the nonexistent word 'larrived,' which is not intelligible on its own and reverses omission into an added initial sound.

rows.jp: ら抜き言葉で、俺は感慨を示した。
rows.en: I mark the occasion with a little grammatical shortcut.

ghs.en: I expressed my strong feelings by unnecessarily making a word start with "la".
ghs.assessment: The Japanese explicitly comments on ra-nuki, a form made by dropping a ra syllable. The English says a sound was added to the start of a word, reversing the linguistic mechanism it purports to explain.

highlights.text: by unnecessarily making a word start with "la"

ghs.en: Taichi: "Gh'yah!"

rows.jp: 足首が曲がった。転倒しかける。
rows.en: My ankle twists. I nearly go down.

ghs.en: My ankle bent. I go tumbling down.

rows.jp: 咄嗟にベルトに仕込んだルパン・ワイヤーを伸ばし枝に巻きつける……ということができたらイカスのだが、普通に転んだ。
rows.en: It'd be cool if I could shoot out the Lupin wire hidden in my belt and whip it around a branch... but I just fall over.

ghs.en: Instantaneously I latched onto a nearby tree branch the Lupin Wire built into my belt... or that's what I'd do if I was that clever, and instead fell down normally.

rows.jp: こういう時は素直に転んだ方がいい。
rows.en: At times like this, it is better to let yourself fall.

ghs.en: At times like this, just up and falling down is best.
Ukemi.
Taichi: "...hm?"

rows.jp: 地面をよくよく見ると。

ghs.en: I look very very close to the ground as I move.
Footprints.

rows.jp: 祠の前から一直線、帯状に足跡が重なっている。
rows.en: A straight band of overlapping prints runs out from the shrine.

ghs.en: A straight line of footprints from the front of the hokora, overlapping, forming a belt shape.

rows.jp: 何十往復すればこんなことになるのだろう。
rows.en: How many dozens of trips back and forth would it take to leave tracks like this?

ghs.en: This is what would happen when you go around and around many times.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese asks how many dozens of round trips would be needed to produce so many overlapping tracks. The English turns the question into a generic assertion and omits both the round trips and the scale.
ghs.remedy: How many dozens of round trips would it take to leave tracks like this?

highlights.text: This is what would happen when you go around and around many times.

rows.jp: 靴跡そのものを調べてみる。
rows.en: I examine the shoe prints themselves.

ghs.en: I investigate one of the shoeprints.
Size is around 27.
Same as mine.
Brand and model too, I would say.
Taichi: "......"
Same shoes as mine.
These are not Tomoki's shoes.
They are not Sakuraba's either.

rows.jp: 女子に２７なんてのはいないはずだ。
rows.en: None of the girls should wear a Japanese size 27.

ghs.en: I can't really believe a woman would be a size 27.

rows.jp: 全員の身体データを把握している俺が言うのだから間違いはない。
rows.en: I know everyone's physical data, so there is no mistaking it.

ghs.en: I have a firm grasp on all members' body data, therefore I can say that with no mistake.

rows.jp: 記憶喪失の俺か、俺の靴を使用した何者かが、つけた跡ということになる。
rows.en: Which means either I made them and don't remember, or someone else did in shoes just like mine.

ghs.en: Perhaps by me with memory loss, perhaps by someone using my shoes, but somehow these shoeprints were made.

rows.en: But what business would they have at the shrine?

ghs.en: But to do what at the hokora?

rows.jp: 思案に没頭しようとした時―――
rows.en: Just as I am about to sink into thought―――

ghs.en: I tried to immerse myself in thought---
ghs.assessment: The authoritative Japanese is only a silent exclamation of sudden alarm. The English invents a full narration about trying to think and replaces the reaction entirely.

highlights.text: I tried to immerse myself in thought---

ghs.en: I caught a whiff of blood,
a faint smell of blood.

rows.jp: 引き寄せられて、茂みに分け入っていく。
rows.en: Drawn toward it, I push into the undergrowth.

ghs.en: Pulling myself towards it, I force my way into the thicket.

rows.en: My danger sense goes off immediately.

ghs.en: Immediately a warning signal sounded.

rows.jp: 太一袋からナイフを取り出す。
rows.en: I take a knife from the Taichi Bag.

ghs.en: I took out the knife from the Taichi bag.

rows.jp: クリスリーブの大型ナイフだ。

ghs.en: It was a large Chris Reeve knife.

rows.jp: ここまで来ると短剣に近い。
rows.en: At this size, it is almost a dagger.

ghs.en: Large to the point where it is close to a dagger.

rows.jp: もちろん携行は犯罪だが。
rows.en: Carrying it is a crime, of course.

ghs.en: Of course carrying it is a crime, but,

rows.jp: 犯罪という概念はなくなっている。
rows.en: But the very concept of crime is gone now.

ghs.en: the very concept of crime was no more.

rows.jp: 俺も所持は禁じられている。
rows.en: I am forbidden to possess one all the same.

ghs.en: I am also forbidden from being in possession of it,
but,

rows.jp: 認められはしないだろうが、護身のため俺はこれを必要としている。
rows.en: No one would approve, but I need this to defend myself.

ghs.en: even if it won't be recognized, this is something I need for my own protection.

rows.jp: 人に攻撃され続ける恐怖を知っているからだ。
rows.en: Because I know the terror of being attacked, again and again.

ghs.en: Because I know the horror of being repeatedly attacked by people.
I strained my ears.
I make the perceptions sharper.
I walk slowly.

rows.jp: 探すのは違和感だけだ。
rows.en: All I'm looking for is something that feels wrong.

ghs.en: The only thing I can search for is the sense of physical discomfort.
ghs.assessment: In this search, iwakan means an anomaly or something out of place that might reveal a hidden threat. 'Physical discomfort' turns the external irregularity into a bodily sensation and misstates what the narrator is scanning for.
ghs.remedy: anything that feels out of place

ghs.en: Found it.

rows.jp: 俺の目は違和感を逃がさない。
rows.en: My eyes never miss what does not belong.

ghs.en: That sense of physical discomfort will never escape from my eyes.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the narrator's eyes do not miss anomalies. The English again makes the anomaly a bodily discomfort and then makes that sensation the subject escaping from his eyes, producing an incoherent relation.
ghs.remedy: My eyes never miss anything out of place.

highlights.text: That sense of physical discomfort will never escape from my eyes.

rows.jp: 慎重に迂回して、根本に近づく。
rows.en: I circle around carefully and approach its base.

ghs.en: I prudently walk around it, to near the tree roots.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says he circles carefully and approaches the base of the suspicious setup. It does not identify tree roots; the English introduces a tree-specific target and obscures that he is inspecting the trap.

ghs.en: ...a crossbow trap?

rows.jp: 小型のクロスボウを利用している。

ghs.en: It uses a very small crossbow.

rows.jp: 奥に入ろうとすると作動するわけだ。
rows.en: Trying to go deeper would trigger it.

ghs.en: This would trigger on anyone trying to go any deeper.
It's not yet been fired.

rows.jp: こんなことをしそうな人物に、心当たりは一人しかない。
rows.en: I can think of only one person who would do something like this.

ghs.en: I happen to know of only one person with the personality trait to do this sort of thing.

rows.jp: ワイヤーを切断し、クロスボウから矢を外す。
rows.en: I cut the trigger wire and remove the bolt from the crossbow.

ghs.en: Disconnect the wire, remove the bolt from the crossbow.

rows.jp: かなり慎重に隠蔽してあった。

ghs.en: It was fairly cautiously concealed.

rows.jp: 仕掛ける位置もうまい。

ghs.en: Setup location is also skillful.

rows.jp: 少し目視できる、段差の手前だ。
rows.en: It sits just before a visible drop in the ground.

ghs.en: Just in front of the tall step of the hokora, barely visible.

rows.jp: 段差に注意をはらっていると、死ぬことになるわけだ。
rows.en: Pay attention to the drop and you die.

ghs.en: If I gone to the step without paying attention, I would have been dead.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says the victim dies if attention is directed to the visible step, because that distraction hides the trap. The English says death follows from not paying attention to the step, reversing the trap's design as well as using an ungrammatical verb form.
ghs.remedy: If you focus on the step, the trap kills you.

highlights.text: If I gone to the step without paying attention, I would have been dead.

rows.jp: 陰湿で、確実さを求めた罠。
rows.en: A vicious trap built for a sure kill.

ghs.en: That's reliable hunting trap, malicious in intent.

rows.jp: 奥を確認してやろうじゃないか、曜子先生。
rows.en: Let's see what lies farther in, Professor Yoko.

ghs.en: How about ascertaining what's back there, then, Youko-sensei?

rows.jp: 少し進むと、ワイヤートラップが仕掛けられていた。
rows.en: A little farther on, I find a wire trap.

ghs.en: I advanced a bit, and found a wire trap laid out.

rows.jp: スネアだ。足を吊られると、頭上から石が落ちてくる。
rows.en: A snare. Once it hoists you by the foot, rocks come down from overhead.

ghs.en: It's a snare. If feet tripped it, a rock would fall from overhead.
Disarmed.
The warning signal waned.
Does this mean there's no more?

rows.jp: それでも用心深く進む。
rows.en: I advance cautiously all the same.

ghs.en: I proceed warily nevertheless.

rows.jp: 最後の草むらを抜けると、隠されるように、曜子ちゃんが死んでいた。
rows.en: When I push through the last thicket, I find Yoko lying dead, as though hidden away.

ghs.en: I come out of the last bush and there, as if she were concealed, Youko-chan had died.

rows.jp: この感情をどう形容したらいいんだろう。
rows.en: How am I supposed to describe this feeling?

ghs.en: What description could I even use for the emotion I have.
It is different from shock.
It is different from anger.

rows.jp: 悲しみでも、悲嘆でもない。

ghs.en: Nor is it sadness, nor even grief.
A torrent of something I can't describe,
that swirls inside of me into an eddy.
Youko-chan... had died.

rows.jp: 胸を中心に血が広がっている。
rows.en: Blood has spread outward from the center of her chest.

ghs.en: Blood spread into the center of her chest.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says blood has spread outward with the chest as its center, describing the visible extent around the wound. The English reverses that direction and says the blood moved into the chest's center.
ghs.remedy: Blood had spread out from the center of her chest.

highlights.text: Blood spread into the center of her chest.

ghs.en: It is stale blood.

rows.jp: かたまって変色し、黒ずんでいる。

ghs.en: it's clumped and solidified, its color changed, darkened.
I touch. Cold.

rows.jp: 死後数日。硬直してしまっていた。
rows.en: It looks like she has been dead for days. Her body has gone stiff.

ghs.en: Days after death. Rigor mortis it seems.

rows.jp: しかし腐敗している様子はない。
rows.en: But there is no sign of decay.

ghs.en: However, there's no trace of decay.

rows.jp: それも奇妙な話だが……まあ置いておこう。
rows.en: That is strange too... but I will set it aside.

ghs.en: That is also so very strange but... well, I'll set that aside.

rows.jp: 「……曜子ちゃん、死んじゃったのか」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...so you died after all, Youko-chan, did you."

rows.jp: 美しい骸に、話しかける。
rows.en: I speak to the beautiful corpse.

ghs.en: I talk to this beautiful husk.

rows.jp: 一番死とは遠かったはずなのに。
rows.en: She was supposed to be farther from death than anyone.

ghs.en: But she should have been the furthest from death.
I straighten her hair.
Taichi: "Careless weren't you."
Yet there is no reply.

rows.jp: 俺が話しかけたら、小動物みたく喜んだ。
rows.en: Whenever I spoke to her, she'd light up like some small animal.

ghs.en: When I spoke to her, she was happy like a little animal.

rows.en: Even though I treated her coldly.

ghs.en: Even though I was cruel,

rows.jp: 小さなウサギみたいに。

ghs.en: she was just like a tiny little rabbit.

rows.jp: ……本当は、獅子にも狼にもなれた彼女だ。
rows.en: ...Though in truth, she could be a lion or a wolf.

ghs.en: ...truth is, she had become more like a lion or a big bad wolf.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says she was in truth capable of becoming a lion or a wolf, contrasting that potential with the rabbit image. The English says she had already become like them and adds the fairy-tale register 'big bad.'
ghs.remedy: she was capable of becoming a lion or a wolf.

highlights.text: she had become more like a lion or a big bad wolf.

ghs.en: Taichi: "What a surprise."
My sight clouded.
Taichi: "...hm?"

rows.en: I touch the corner of my eye.

ghs.en: I try touching the outer corners of my eyes.
Tears,
and plenty of them.
There is no sadness,

rows.jp: ただ顔の筋肉だけが引きつって、涙を絞り出していた。
rows.en: Only the muscles in my face are spasming, squeezing out tears.

ghs.en: just a cramp of the muscles of the face, that squeeze out tears,
without end.

rows.jp: 「うわ、すげ……ぼろぼろ出てきてる」
rows.en: “Whoa, look at that... They're pouring out.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Whoa, 'mazing... they're coming out all rain-like!"
Inexplicable.

rows.jp: 肉体は悲しんでいるのかも知れない。

ghs.en: The flesh appears sad, or something, I'm not sure,
but the heart...
Ahhh.
Half of my body had died.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese uses 'half of me' for a person experienced as part of oneself. 'Half of my body' literalizes it as physical anatomy and loses the relational meaning.

highlights.text: Half of my body had died.

ghs.en: Kiri: "...Senpai... you..."
KIRI!!!
Miki: "..."
And Miki too.

rows.jp: 咄嗟にナイフを……隠しても意味がない。
rows.en: My first instinct is to hide the knife... but there is no point.

ghs.en: Concealing my knife at once... is meaningless.
I was already seen.

rows.jp: そして……誤解されるだろう。
rows.en: And... they are going to misunderstand.

ghs.en: And then... likely misunderstood.
Kiri: "Mur-... murderer... I knew it..."
I knew it.
Kiri: "Are you the killer?"
Taichi: "...no I'm not!"

rows.jp: 「だって、ナイフ持ってるじゃないですか……」

ghs.en: Kiri: "But isn't that a knife in your hand...?"

rows.jp: 「茂みに入るから、持ってただけだ」
rows.en: “I only had it out because I was going into the undergrowth.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I had to get through the ticket, that's why I do, no other reason."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says he was only holding the knife because he was entering the thicket. The English mistranslates 'thicket' as 'ticket' and leaves the explanation grammatically incoherent.
ghs.remedy: I only had it out because I was going into the thicket.

highlights.text: I had to get through the ticket, that's why I do, no other reason.

rows.jp: 「ほら、彼女の傷口見てみろよ。矢傷だ」
rows.en: “Look at her wound. It's from an arrow.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Look, come and see her wound. It's an arrow shot."
Kiri: "...I will not be going... not there."
Making a wide circle at a distance,

rows.jp: 霧は俺を注視していた。

ghs.en: Kiri was observing me intently.

rows.jp: 油断する気はないらしい。
rows.en: Apparently, she has no intention of letting her guard down.

ghs.en: She has no intention of letting her guard down.

rows.jp: 「……さっきまで……笑って話してたのに……裏では、平気でそういうことをするんだ……」
rows.en: “...You were laughing and talking with us just moments ago... and behind our backs, you can do something like this without a second thought...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "...just until now... you were smiling and talking and then... but out of sight, you were doing this, in cold blood..."
She spat at me.
Kiri: "You are insane!"
Miki: "......Senpai."

rows.jp: 美希もショックを受けている。

ghs.en: Miki also seems to have been shocked.

rows.jp: 無念そうな、思い詰めたような。そんな顔だ。
rows.en: Regretful. Tormented. Something like that—that's how she looks.

ghs.en: Regretful and tormented over this. That's what her face said.
Kiri: "Let's go, Miki."
Miki: "Ah, yes..."

rows.jp: 二人は引き返していく。
rows.en: The two of them turn back.

ghs.en: The two retrace their steps,
leaving me behind.
Taichi: "But that wasn't me."
Oh, whatever, who cares.
Youko-chan had died.

rows.jp: 存外、俺は衝撃を受けていたらしい。
rows.en: Apparently, the shock has hit me harder than I expected.

ghs.en: Unexpectedly, I too seem to have struck with a big impact.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that, contrary to expectation, the narrator seems to have been deeply shocked. The English makes him the ungrammatical agent of 'have struck' rather than the person affected by the shock.
ghs.remedy: Apparently, I was more deeply shocked than I'd expected.

highlights.text: I too seem to have struck with a big impact.

rows.jp: 思考はぼんやりとして、なかなか明晰さを取り戻してくれなかった。
rows.en: My thoughts remain hazy, stubbornly refusing to regain their clarity.

ghs.en: My thoughts were lax and aimless, and would not allow me a quick or ready return to clarity.

rows.jp: それが俺の、彼女に対する慟哭だった。
rows.en: That was my lament for her.

ghs.en: And that... was the lamentation I held for her.
